# Business Tips Content Marketing Tips for Small Businesses

Content marketing is one of the most effective inbound marketing strategies a business can adopt. Posting and distributing fresh content on your business website gets your website noticed and your brand known.

Almost any type of business can benefit from a content marketing campaign. However, some small business owners shy away from this inexpensive form of marketing because they are unsure where to begin.

So, if you keep putting off writing your first piece of marketing content, read on. Here are nine tips to help small business owners make the most of content marketing.

### 1) Define Your Target Audience

It is best to start a content marketing campaign by defining who you want to attract to your website. You will want to post content that will appeal to potential customers. But do you know who your typical customers are? Do you understand what drives the people who buy your products, what their interests are, and where they are most likely to hang out on the web? Develop a picture of who your typical customers are and then produce content that will appeal to those people.

### 2) Research Keywords

The next step is to consider the keywords for which you want to gain a search engine ranking. Keywords are the search terms that people use when looking for something on Google or other search engines. It is usually best to refine your keywords so that they reflect exactly what your business offers. So, suppose you own a roof repair business in Wilmington, Delaware, for example. In that case, one of your keywords might be ‘roofing contractor Wilmington, Delaware’. Then you must consider all the other terms that someone needing a roof repair might use to find a roofer, like roof repairs, roof replacement, roof storm damage repair, etc.

### 3) Check Out Your Competition

One of the things that often hold people back from producing marketing content is they can’t think of anything to write. If you need some topic inspiration, the best place to start is to research what your competitors post on their blog and social media accounts. When you look at your competitors’ content, note the topics and the posts’ formats. Look at what keywords they are targeting, too. It would not be advisable to follow what your competition is doing blindly. Even so, reviewing your competitors’ content marketing strategies is a good starting point to get you thinking about topics for your posts.

### 4) Decide Who Will Develop Your Content

Someone in your business will need to be responsible for your content marketing campaign. Someone will need to take charge of content creation and posting. One of the big mistakes that small companies make with content marketing is that they begin with a flourish of content but then stop posting because of time constraints. It takes time for content marketing to work, and you must post consistently and regularly. So, if you don’t have the time to produce the content, it would be best to delegate the task or hire a freelancer to do the job.

### 5) Create a Content Calendar

A content creation calendar will give you deadlines and a schedule of content that needs to be produced. Looking ahead will also help you plan content for the various seasons and holidays. When deciding on topics, bear in mind that content marketing is not all about selling. Content marketing is about creating brand awareness, drawing people to your website, and demonstrating your expertise in your field. So, think about entertaining and informative topics that will attract the right audience. The subjects you choose will also need to be suitable for your chosen keywords.

### 6) Test Different Formats

You are not limited to standard format blog posts. You could also post videos, infographics, in-depth articles, tutorials, and more. So, mix it up a little and see what goes down best with your target audience. You will also find that different formats and topics work better on different platforms. The best way to find out what works for your business is to experiment with various forms and structures of posts and track the results.

### 7) Make Your Content Easy to Share

If you haven’t already done so, install share buttons on your blog, and share your content in your own social media accounts. It can also be helpful to allow comments on your blog posts to encourage user interaction. If you allow comments on your posts, make sure you put some time aside to respond to comments. Content marketing becomes incredibly powerful when it becomes a talking point, and the content gets shared.

### 8) Monitor Results

Content marketing may not result in an immediate increase in sales. It may take time for someone who discovers your brand through your content to become a customer. Even so, you will be able to track the success of your content marketing campaign by monitoring visitor numbers to your website and content shares. Monitoring content metrics will also help you discover which type of posts generate the most interest. In time, the increased brand awareness your content marketing is creating will lead to sales.

### 9) Don’t Give Up Too Soon

Any marketing strategy takes time to yield results, and content marketing is no exception. It could take 3-6 months of regular posting before you begin to see any results. It will probably take you that long to identify the types of posts that are the most effective, too. So, be patient, keep on posting, and refine your posts according to what you discover works best. If you continue to post valuable content, it will increase brand awareness and sales in the long run.

### Conclusion

Content marketing is a cost-effective way to generate greater interest in your brand. However, to make this kind of marketing work, you must know who your customers are and post content that will interest those people. It is also crucial that you post consistently and don’t give up on the idea too soon.

This comes as no surprise, considering a business’s budget constraints may not be top of mind for consumers when browsing online or in person.

[Traditional advertising methods](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/marketing/advertising-guide/?sa=cl) can be costly and may not always yield desired results. While traditional marketing relies on advertisements and sales pitches, content marketing works to educate, entertain, and inspire prospects. # Content Marketing for Small Business: A Guide to Getting Relevant Leads

January 20, 2026

![Content Marketing for Small Business](https://d1rv23qj5kas56.cloudfront.net/lp-payload-cms/media/Content-Marketing-for-Small-Business.jpg?2026-09-15T08%3A31%3A42.992Z)

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.webnode.com%2Fblog%2Fcontent-marketing-for-small-businesses%2F)[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.webnode.com%2Fblog%2Fcontent-marketing-for-small-businesses%2F)[](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.webnode.com%2Fblog%2Fcontent-marketing-for-small-businesses%2F&text=Content%20Marketing%20for%20Small%20Business%3A%20A%20Guide%20to%20Getting%20Relevant%20Leads)[](https://wa.me/?text=Content%20Marketing%20for%20Small%20Business%3A%20A%20Guide%20to%20Getting%20Relevant%20Leads%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.webnode.com%2Fblog%2Fcontent-marketing-for-small-businesses%2F)

Running a small business is a lot. You’re trying to serve clients, answer emails, manage staff, and still somehow “do marketing”. The last thing you need is another vague tip like “post more on social media”.

**You’ll learn:**

*   [What is content marketing](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#what-is-content-marketing)
*   [How content marketing is different from traditional advertising](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#how-content-marketing-is-different-from-traditional-advertising)
*   [The 5 C’s of content marketing](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#the-5-c-s-of-content-marketing)
*   [Step 1 – Know your audience](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#step-1-know-your-audience-and-their-real-problems)
*   [Step 2 – Map the customer journey](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#step-2-map-the-customer-journey-from-first-question-to-booking)
*   [Step 3 – Set goals and KPIs](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#step-3-set-goals-and-kpis-before-you-create-any-content)
*   [Step 4 – Choose content formats and channels](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#step-4-choose-content-formats-and-channels-that-fit-your-customers)
*   [DIY content vs. freelancer vs. agency](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#diy-content-vs-freelancer-vs-agency)
*   [How much does content marketing cost for SMBs](https://www.webnode.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/#how-much-does-content-marketing-cost-for-smbs)

Content marketing can genuinely help you **get better customers**, not just more clicks. But only if it’s done with a clear plan.

Instead of guessing, let’s look at how small businesses really use content marketing today – and what they say works for them.

*   **Only 57%** of 702 small businesses surveyed (60% B2C vs. 40% B2B) **report doing any content marketing**. ([Servicedirect](https://servicedirect.com/resources/small-business-content-marketing-survey-data/), 2022)
*   44% of respondents said **generating new customers was the primary goal**, while 33% hoped to **improve customer retention and loyalty,** and 20% wanted to **increase brand awareness**. ([Servicedirect](https://servicedirect.com/resources/small-business-content-marketing-survey-data/), 2022)
*   **29% of B2C marketers say their content marketing is “very successful” and 52% call it “moderately successful”** – proof that this approach works when done consistently. ([Taboola](https://www.taboola.com/marketing-hub/content-marketing-statistics/), 2024)

Yet many small businesses never start – or they publish a few random posts and stop because they don’t see results. This guide is here to change that.

## What is content marketing

**Content marketing** is the practice of creating helpful articles, videos, emails, and social media posts that:

*   answer your customers’ questions,
*   solve their problems,
*   guide them toward your business.

Instead of pushing “Buy now!” everywhere, you **show your expertise first**. That way, when people are ready to buy, they already trust you.

> **Example**
> 
> *   A **hairdresser** publishes a guide on “How to fix orange hair after box dye (and when you need a professional)”.
> *   A **plumber** records a short video explaining “What to do when your sink is blocked – before you call a plumber”.
> *   A **vet clinic** shares a blog post on “Early signs your dog might be in pain – and what to do next”.

In each case, the **content**:

1.  **Helps the reader** with a real-life situation.
2.  **Provides value** by showcasing what you’re doing.
3.  **Makes it easy** to contact you for professional help.

### How content marketing is different from traditional advertising

Traditional advertising (online or offline) is usually:

*   short,
*   pushy,
*   and focused on “buy now” messages.

Content marketing is more like a conversation:

*   “Here’s how we can help you.”
*   “Here are your options.”
*   “Here’s what to watch out for.”

Both have their place. Advertising can bring quick attention. But for **trust, loyalty and long-term customers**, content marketing is hard to beat.

Research backs this up. According to the Content Marketing Institute, marketers consistently say [content marketing helps create brand awareness, generate leads, nurture audiences and even drive sales](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/content-marketing-strategy/content-marketing-statistics).

> If you want to go deeper into the basics, our [guide on digital marketing for small businesses](https://www.webnode.com/blog/digital-marketing-small-businesses/) explains how content fits together with SEO, social media and online ads.

## The 5 C’s of content marketing 

Here’s a straightforward way to remember what good content marketing strategy needs. 

**Customer**

Define who your content is for. Be specific: busy parents, pet owners, local shop owners, freelancers, small company CEOs… not “everyone”.

**Clarity** 

Use simple language and clear structure so people immediately understand what you offer and what they should do next.

**Consistency**

Keep your message, tone and promises aligned across your website, social media, emails and in-person communication. It’s less about posting every day, week or month and more about not confusing your customers.

**Channels**

Focus on the places your customers already use: Google search, email, social media, local listings, messaging apps. You don’t have to be everywhere, just in the right spots.

**Conversion**

results.title: How Content Marketing Can Help Your Small Business: Nine Tips From New York-Based Entrepreneurs
results.markdown:
How Content Marketing Can Help Your Small Business: Nine Tips From New York-Based Entrepreneurs [Skip to main content](https://www.sbdc.uh.edu/sbdc/How_Content_Marketing_Can_Help_Your_Small_Business.asp#main-content) [Skip to menu](https://www.sbdc.uh.edu/sbdc/How_Content_Marketing_Can_Help_Your_Small_Business.asp#menu) [Skip to footer](https://www.sbdc.uh.edu/sbdc/How_Content_Marketing_Can_Help_Your_Small_Business.asp#footer)

**How Content Marketing Can Help Your Small** **Business****: Nine Tips From New York-Based Entrepreneurs**   
  

**![](/images/sbdc/Blog%20Photos/How%20Content%20Marketing%20Can%20Help%20Your%20Small%20Business%20Nine%20Tips%20From%20New%20York-Based%20Entrepreneurs%20UH%20SBDC.jpg)  
**

  

Content marketing is making a real impact on small businesses looking to reach customers at an affordable price. Creating content that resonates with your customers can help generate interest in your brand while boosting your expertise in your industry at the same time. 

When content marketing is done right, it can really help take a business to the next level. Even in a highly competitive market such as New York, the right content marketing efforts can help you stand out from your rivals and become more visible to your target audience. 

To help you take advantage of content marketing the smartest way possible, we asked members of Forbes New York Business Council to weigh in with their top content marketing tips for small businesses in New York. Here’s what they had to say:

**1\. Give Them What They Want** 

As a business owner, it’s really easy to want to push your own agenda as to what you show the customer, but if they love someone that you may not necessarily love, give them more of that! It’s not about you, it’s about what customers want. Give them what they want and they’ll be back for more. Stick to what works. - Hoda Mahmoodzadegan, Molly’s Milk Truck + F'in Delicious Beverages

**2\. Be Original** One of the worst things I see when I look to patronize or connect with another business is if their social media is full of stock photos or is obviously being run by a third party. To me it shows that they don't take pride in what they actually do in their own small business. Show what you do and what a great job you do at it. Seeing someone else's work doesn't make me want to go to you. - Edward Alvarez, Edward A Alvarez, DDS, PC/NYCLaserDentist

**3\. Don't Be Afraid To Share What You Know** I used to think that everything I learned in 15 years designing stores and interiors should not be shared. After all, clients hire me for that knowledge, so why give it away? In the past year I started writing for Forbes or for my blog, giving out all my "secrets", and I got a lot of exposure from it. Clients now come because of these writings. - Sergio Mannino, Sergio Mannino Studio, we design interiors and we create brands 

**4\. Leverage The Power Of Audio** 

I admit I’m biased, but I think podcasting is one of the greatest ways to get your message out, no matter how big your business. All of your production and distribution needs are right there on your phone. It’s infinitely less costly than video, and it’s a medium that is perfectly catered to niche topics and audiences. - Francesco Baschieri, Voxnest 

**5\. Identify Your Target Audience And Their Needs** 

Identify exactly who you’re speaking to and what keeps them up at night. Then think about how something you are knowledgeable about can give them a leg up. And don’t be afraid to give away the secret sauce. Some of the most successful business consultancies in the world give their entire process away in book form (StoryBrand, EOS, E-Myth Worldwide, etc.). - Tom Conlon, North Street 

**6\. Create Meaningful, Entertaining Content** 

Keep your audience engaged, curious and wanting to learn more. Write interesting articles, create entertaining video and share your knowledge as freely as possible. Content allows potential clients to get to know you as a person and your company's brand. - Jill Strickman, GENUINE: The Real People Company 

**7\. Focus On Providing Value** 

Digital content is often the first impression consumed by your consumer. Offer value, clearly represent your brand and develop a strategy built for your consumer for every platform. Here are a few questions to help develop a content strategy: 1) Does it offer value to the consumer? 2) Does it communicate what, why and how? 3) Is it confusing or clear? 4) Is it consistent with the brand message? - Rob Taormina, TalkIQ Media 

**8\. Highlight Unique Company Endeavors** 

Highlight unique and authentic company endeavors. Two unique and authentic endeavors we've highlighted include a social campaign for women's month, which highlights both our team members and female clients through various platforms, and an upcoming podcast entitled "The Brick Wall," which stems from a team phrase used to power through even the biggest challenges in the office space. - Warren H. Cohn, HeraldPR 

**9\. Create Solutions For Your Ideal Customers** 

As a small business, you need to differentiate yourself from competitors. But, when creating content, be careful not to talk about yourself. Once you have identified who your ideal customers are and where they are consuming content, you should create content that is focused on them, not you. Create solutions for them—provide a "what's in it for me" and your content marketing will soar. - Andy Seibert, Imprint
